name: BSP_MSTGun_RingMuzzleOrigin
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc2_gun_platform_arc, read-only analysis. __thiscall(gun)(float* out, const float* in), body 006FE160-006FE38D; gun vtable slot 1E0h for class 27h, overriding the 006E3DC0 identity copy. Builds a basis from the input direction through BSP_Matrix_BuildLookAt and offsets the origin by descriptor+D0h times cos and sin of (gun+44Ch * 2pi / muzzleNodeCount), the count coming from the descriptor's +9Ch/+A0h node vector. This is the ring that spreads a salvo mount's barrels. | CORRECTION, packet cc7_gun_mount_positions: the name is wrong, the arithmetic is right. Slot 1E0h's in/out is the shot DIRECTION, not a muzzle origin. The only dispatch of slot 1E0h in .text is 0072FE63-0072FE74 in BSP_Gun_SpawnShotAndEffects, whose in is that routine's arg3 - the triple BSP_Gun_Fire fills at 0073022A/0073023C/00730249 from row 2 of the mount node's world matrix (gun[+3CCh]+0F0h+20h) and then perturbs with the Throw cone at 00730654..0073075E. The world muzzle point is a separate argument, arg1, built at 00730762..007307FC. Corroborated inside this body: 006FE1A4 passes in to BSP_Matrix_BuildLookAt as the look-at TARGET with the eye pinned to the triple zeroed at 006FE192-006FE19E, which is only meaningful for a direction; and the ring radius class+0D0h is the Lua key MultiBulletConeAngle (00CFE880, stored at 00732B1C), an angle on a direction. So 006FE160 spreads a sub-type 27h shot cone per barrel, not the barrels across the hull. A better name would be BSP_MSTGun_BarrelConeDirection. docs/GUN_MOUNT_POSITIONS.md section 6.
